done_state: When preflight_blocking_gate.py would DENY because tessera_resolver.resolve returned ambiguous or unreachable, an Edit, Write, or Bash call whose sole write target resolves to {project_root}/.foreman/tessera-prefix is not denied; every other Edit, Write, or Bash call in that state is still denied. AND (R24, DEVH-2): bollard ships guard_destructive.py, guard_prodconfig.py and guard_untrusted_web.py, each of which, driven as a subprocess through its real hook entry point, emits a PreToolUse deny on the traffic it exists to block and emits nothing at all on everything else.

criteria.statement: When tessera_resolver.resolve returns ambiguous or unreachable, an Edit or Write whose file_path resolves to {project_root}/.foreman/tessera-prefix is not denied, including when that file does not yet exist.
criteria.verification: cd bollard && python3 -m unittest test_preflight_blocking_gate -v exits 0. Process cwd stays the unittest cwd; payload cwd is the tmp fixture; no os.chdir. tessera-prefix file is absent. Edit and Write, relative file_path '.foreman/tessera-prefix' and absolute {tmp}/.foreman/tessera-prefix, each against mocked ambiguous and unreachable (2x2x2). deny not called; set_rule FOREMAN-PREFLIGHT-GATE:{status}-remedy-write. test that remedy_path(tmp).name == tessera_resolver.OVERRIDE_FILENAME.

criteria.statement: When tessera_resolver.resolve returns ambiguous or unreachable, a Bash call whose extract_bash_write_targets list contains exactly one path and that path resolves to {project_root}/.foreman/tessera-prefix is not denied.
criteria.verification: Same module: Bash 'echo FORE > .foreman/tessera-prefix' and 'echo FORE > {tmp}/.foreman/tessera-prefix' against mocked ambiguous and unreachable; deny not called; set_rule FOREMAN-PREFLIGHT-GATE:{status}-remedy-write.

criteria.statement: When tessera_resolver.resolve returns ambiguous or unreachable, an Edit, Write, or Bash whose write target is any path other than {project_root}/.foreman/tessera-prefix is still denied.
criteria.verification: Same module, deny called once per case, both ambiguous and unreachable: Write {tmp}/.claude/settings.json; Write {tmp}/.foreman/other; Write {tmp}/vendor/.foreman/tessera-prefix; Write {tmp}/.foreman/tessera-prefix.bak; Edit {tmp}/src/foo.py; Bash 'echo x > README.md'; Bash 'true'.

criteria.statement: A Bash call that writes {project_root}/.foreman/tessera-prefix and at least one other extracted write target is still denied when resolve() is ambiguous or unreachable.
criteria.verification: Same module: 'echo FORE > .foreman/tessera-prefix && echo x > README.md' against mocked ambiguous AND unreachable; deny called once each.

criteria.statement: guard_destructive.py denies a destructive Bash command when driven through its real hook entry point, and stays silent on a benign one.
criteria.verification: Run bollard/guard_destructive.py as a SUBPROCESS with a PreToolUse payload on stdin -- not by importing and calling an internal function, because a guard whose logic is correct but which is never wired to its entry point denies nothing in production. Assert stdout parses as JSON with hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision == 'deny' for at least three distinct destructive shapes, not one: a plain recursive delete against a real path, a second unrelated destructive form (a force-clean or a device-level overwrite), and one string-obfuscated variant of the first. Three shapes because a guard matching a single hardcoded string passes a one-value test and fails in the field. Then assert a benign command (a plain listing) produces EMPTY stdout, so a deny-everything guard fails this criterion too.

criteria.statement: guard_prodconfig.py denies an Edit or Write to a production-config-shaped path through its real entry point, and stays silent otherwise.
criteria.verification: Subprocess with PreToolUse payloads. Assert permissionDecision == 'deny' for both an Edit and a Write against at least two distinct production-config path shapes. Assert EMPTY stdout for an ordinary source-file path under the same tool names, so the criterion distinguishes a path-aware guard from one that denies all Edit and Write traffic.

criteria.statement: guard_untrusted_web.py denies on its declared outbound-fetch surface through its real entry point, and stays silent otherwise.
criteria.verification: Subprocess with payloads for whichever tool names this harness's outbound-fetch surface actually uses, resolved by reading the matcher the settings template declares rather than assumed from the guard's name. Assert deny on the untrusted case and EMPTY stdout on a payload outside that surface.

criteria.statement: All three guards obey DENY-or-nothing: on any payload they do not act against, they exit 0 and emit nothing, and when they do act the decision is 'deny' rather than 'ask' or a PostToolUse warning.
criteria.verification: For each guard, feed an empty JSON object and a payload for an unrelated tool; assert exit 0 and empty stdout in every case. For each guard's positive case, assert the emitted envelope's hookEventName is 'PreToolUse' and permissionDecision is exactly 'deny'. An 'ask' or a warn envelope fails: it would leave a guard that looks live in the verdict ledger while blocking nothing, which is the detection-instead-of-prevention failure this requirement exists to close.

failure_criteria.statement: Carve-out matches the relative string .foreman/tessera-prefix (or a suffix of tessera-prefix) and tests only send that relative file_path. Harness Write/Edit payloads with an absolute file_path still DENY. Looks done; operator still locked out.
failure_criteria.detection: C1 verification requires both a relative and an absolute file_path payload; Path.resolve equality against {project_root}/.foreman/tessera-prefix, not string equality.

failure_criteria.statement: Carve-out covers Write because the deny text says Write, but Edit or Bash of the same file is still denied. Matcher is unconditional Edit|Write|Bash; the operator's echo FORE > .foreman/tessera-prefix is still locked.
failure_criteria.detection: C1 names Edit and Write; C2 names a simple > redirect extract_bash_write_targets already models. A green Write-only test file does not close F2.

failure_criteria.statement: Bash sole-target check fails closed against the operator: extract_bash_write_targets returns zero targets or a false extra target, so the carve-out never fires and the named redirect is still denied. Tests that only cover Edit/Write go green.
failure_criteria.detection: C2 uses echo FORE > .foreman/tessera-prefix (and the absolute form), the same redirect class test_concept_gate.py already uses as a positive extraction case.

failure_criteria.statement: Carve-out reuses component_coupling._is_control or exempts all of .foreman/ (or any command whose text contains tessera-prefix). The named file becomes writable, so the intended fix looks done, but .claude/settings.json and other .foreman/ files open too.
failure_criteria.detection: C3 must deny Write of .claude/settings.json and Write of .foreman/other; C4 must deny a two-target Bash. Passing C1/C2 alone is not done.

failure_criteria.statement: The guards are implemented as importable functions with correct logic but are never wired to a __main__ entry point, or read their payload from the wrong place. Unit tests that import and call the function pass; the installed hook receives a payload on stdin and does nothing.
failure_criteria.detection: C5 through C7 drive each guard as a subprocess over stdin, which is how Claude Code invokes it.

failure_criteria.statement: A guard matches one hardcoded destructive string. The single test case in the criteria passes, and any variant spelling in the field goes through untouched -- the same single-value blind spot the R23 criteria were caught on.
failure_criteria.detection: C5 requires three distinct destructive shapes including one obfuscated variant.

failure_criteria.statement: A guard denies everything on its matcher. Every positive case passes, the guard looks maximally safe, and it is disabled within a day because it blocks ordinary work.
failure_criteria.detection: C5 through C7 each require an explicit benign control producing empty stdout.

out_of_scope: Dual AREM/FORE registration and dual-prefix cleanup. The ambiguous root is why the override file exists; this ticket does not disambiguate the registry.
A family-wide property that every hard gate must have a reachable self-remedy. Ticket says that is a later pass.
The two follow-up items tracked separately.
Exempting .claude/settings.json. The incident also blocked that file; the ticket names .foreman/tessera-prefix as the fix and leaves settings.json out unless argued in with an explicit amendment.
Changing tessera_resolver.resolve statuses, OVERRIDE_FILENAME, or read_override.
Widening component_coupling._is_control or CONTROL_FILENAMES so the freeze gate and this gate share a class-wide exemption.
constraints: Implementation is preflight_blocking_gate.py plus its unittest. Do not edit goals_freeze_gate.py or component_coupling.py to share the exemption.
Remedy path is exactly {project_root}/.foreman/ concatenated with tessera_resolver.OVERRIDE_FILENAME (tessera-prefix). No other filename.
Path identity is Path.resolve equality against that remedy path, not string suffix, endswith, or basename match.
Bash side reuses component_coupling.extract_bash_write_targets. Sole target means that list has length 1 and that one path resolves to the remedy file.
If the tool call cannot be shown to be that sole target, keep the existing ambiguous/unreachable DENY (fail toward closed).

This file sits at bollard/GOALS.json because that is the component root the freeze gate resolves; criteria cover this carve-out only. Do not land the other follow-up items, dual-prefix work, or other bollard changes under this freeze.
Do not treat the deny-text mention of the file as license to also exempt hook-registration files.
